old.name: Edmond Fallot — La Moutarderie
old.label: MUSTARD
old.hook: Burgundy's last independent family mustard mill
old.text: Burgundy's last independent family mustard mill Founded in 1840 by Léon Bouley, a miller who began producing mustard from Burgundian sénevé seeds. In 1928 it was bought by Edmond Fallot (a Doubs-born papermaker and World-War-I veteran) who renamed it and committed to preserving the granite-stone-mill technique. Today the house is run by Marc Désarménien, Edmond's grandson — the last independent family moutarderie in Burgundy, milling about 2,500 tonnes a year on granite millstones near 770 kg each. The slow stone grind keeps the paste cool and the volatile aromatics intact, a method industry abandoned. The tour shows the millstones at work; the Enjoy Fallot boutique sells the full range. A Fallot stand sits at the Saturday market. Where 31 rue du Faubourg Bretonnière Address 31 rue du Faubourg Bretonnière, 21200 Beaune Phone +33 3 80 22 10 02

old.name: Mulot & Petitjean
old.label: PAIN D'ÉPICES
old.hook: Burgundy pain d'épices — a house founded in Dijon in 1796
old.text: Burgundy pain d'épices — a house founded in Dijon in 1796 The Beaune boutique of the Dijon pain d'épices house Mulot & Petitjean, founded 1796 and carrying the Living Heritage Company label. Traditional spice bread, nonnettes — small glazed spice cakes filled with jam — all made by hand. The Burgundian thing to bring home, and the classic partner to foie gras or a strong cheese. Where 1 Place Carnot Address 1 Place Carnot, 21200 Beaune

old.label: CHEESE

old.text: The benchmark maker of AOP Époisses In the village of Époisses, two hours north-west, the Berthaut family makes the benchmark AOP Époisses — the washed-rind, marc-bathed cow's-milk cheese at the pungent edge of the law — plus Soumaintrain and Affidélice. Too far for a casual trip, but the cheese itself reaches the Beaune Saturday market direct. Closed Sundays. old.name: Fromage de Cîteaux — Abbaye de Cîteaux
old.label: CHEESE
old.hook: A washed-rind disc made by Cistercian monks
old.text: A washed-rind disc made by Cistercian monks At the mother abbey of the Cistercian order — founded 1098 — the monks still make the cheese of Cîteaux: a soft, washed-rind disc from the raw milk of their own Montbéliarde herd, sold only at the abbey shop and a few fromagers. Half an hour north of Beaune, easily folded into a Côte de Nuits day. The abbey is a working monastery — silence and respect are expected. Where Saint-Nicolas-lès-Cîteaux — ~25 km north Address Abbaye de Cîteaux, 21700 Saint-Nicolas-lès-Cîteaux Phone +33 3 80 61 11 53

old.name: The ramparts circuit
old.label: CIRCUIT
old.hook: 2.5 km · 1-2 hours · 17 numbered towers and bastions
old.text: 2.5 km · 1-2 hours · 17 numbered towers and bastions The complete medieval wall, walkable almost without a break — 2.5 kilometres past seventeen towers and bastions, much of it garden promenade. Start anywhere; the tourist office on Place de la Halle gives out the map. Walk it at first light from the Rempart des Dames and you will pass nobody. Guided tours July–October open towers normally closed.

old.name: Up into the climats
old.label: VINEYARD
old.hook: 2-3 hours · from the Parc de la Bouzaise into Clos des Mouches & Les Grèves
old.text: 2-3 hours · from the Parc de la Bouzaise into Clos des Mouches & Les Grèves From the Parc de la Bouzaise, take the vineyard lanes west — the Chemin de Battaut, then north — and within 200 metres you are inside the premier crus: Clos des Mouches first, then climbing to Les Grèves on the upper slope. From the top of the chemin the whole Côte de Beaune opens below. No other wine capital lets you walk from a town park into a great vineyard in five minutes.

old.name: Beaune to Meursault by the vines
old.label: HALF-DAY
old.text: ~13 km · 3-3.5 hours · Pommard, Volnay, Meursault The classic Route des Grands Crus walk south: out through Beaune's premier crus into Pommard — the Clos des Épeneaux, the village church — then up to Volnay, perched high and famous for finesse, and down through Monthélie to Meursault, the capital of white Burgundy. Return by bus or taxi if you do not walk back.
